notes: The todo list for making the APK the web (#882): one row per surface in perf/surfaces.json, in the order the work is meant to happen, and the state of each. `state` is `native` only when the row in docs/mobile/screens.json says `enabled: true` and its evidence passes check:visual (ADR-0118); `todo` is a surface the app still opens in the document; `blocked` is one that cannot be worked yet, and `blockedBy` says why. `check:plan` fails when a surface has no row, a row names a surface that does not exist, the two files disagree about what is on, or a ported component in docs/mobile/parity.json belongs to a surface this plan does not know. docs/mobile/parity-plan.md and the tracking issue are generated from this file - do not hand-edit either.

phases.title: Prove the gate
phases.why: The three surfaces that already have a Kotlin screen. Recording both sides here exercises the harness on screens that exist, before a single line of new drawing.

phases.title: Public content
phases.why: Read with no session, so the page can be recorded without the fixture account and a failure is about the screen rather than about data.

phases.title: Sign-in
phases.why: The site is what signs in since #873, and the native card is the one screen a guest sees first. It is also the surface every other signed-in recording depends on.

phases.title: The app's core
phases.why: Home, the account area, notifications and chats: the screens a member opens daily.

phases.title: Products
phases.why: The local-store products, where the app has a real reason to be native: offline writes and a device store behind the same screen.

phases.title: Requests and bookings
phases.why: Forms that end in a server write, so a port has to bring the same validation and the same confirmation as the page.

phases.title: Operator surfaces
phases.why: Listed so nothing is missing, and blocked as one decision: the admin area needs its own security review before any of it is drawn natively (#660).
